title: Native anthropic-messages ingestion: pi clients get mangled requests + wrong-format responses
description:
The pi adapter advertises `api: "anthropic-messages"` for anthropic/bedrock providers, so pi sends NATIVE Anthropic Messages bodies (POST {eavs}/{name}/v1/v1/messages — the Anthropic SDK appends /v1/messages to the advertised baseUrl). But the proxy unconditionally parses incoming bodies as OpenAI chat-completions (`parse_incoming_request` -> `openai::parse_openai_request`, src/transform/mod.rs:182-184) whenever `needs_transform()` (src/proxy.rs:548-549), and returns OpenAI-format SSE (`build_openai_sse_response`, src/proxy.rs:1120+).

Consequences for a native anthropic request: top-level `system` is dropped (parser only reads system-role messages with string content), anthropic `tools` (input_schema) don't parse, tool_use/tool_result/thinking content blocks are mangled, and the response comes back in OpenAI SSE which the Anthropic SDK cannot parse. `parse_anthropic_request` exists (src/transform/anthropic.rs:239) but has ZERO callers — dead code.

Fix: detect native Messages requests (api_path ends with /v1/messages, including the double /v1/v1/messages from baseUrl+SDK path concat) and pass them through untransformed when the upstream speaks anthropic (Anthropic, Bedrock w/ SigV4 body rules), same as /v1/responses is handled today (src/proxy.rs:543-544). Forward client `anthropic-beta` headers (pi sends fine-grained-tool-streaming / interleaved-thinking betas, and OAuth adds claude-code-20250219,oauth-2025-04-20). Mind upstream URL: base ends with /v1 and remainder starts with /v1 -> avoid api.anthropic.com/v1/v1/messages. Optionally use parse_anthropic_request + an anthropic SSE builder to translate anthropic-format clients to non-anthropic upstreams. Usage/cost tracking must parse anthropic SSE (parse_stream_chunk machinery exists) while relaying bytes unmodified.
close_reason: Implemented: native /v1/messages (incl. /v1/v1/messages) passthrough for Anthropic providers — no OpenAI-format parsing, anthropic SSE relayed as-is, client anthropic-beta forwarded, Claude Code OAuth identity/tool transforms applied on the native body, anthropic usage extraction for virtual keys. e2e test e2e_native_anthropic_messages_passthrough.

title: Native google-generative-ai path broken: /v1 routing artifact yields v1beta/v1/models 404
description:
pi's google-generative-ai api (@google/genai with httpOptions.baseUrl = advertised baseUrl, apiVersion="") posts to {eavs}/{name}/v1/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse. In the proxy, api_path "/v1/models/...:streamGenerateContent" accidentally matches is_passthrough_endpoint (api_path.starts_with("/v1/models/"), src/proxy.rs:537-539) — that check was meant for OpenAI /v1/models/{id} lookups. Passthrough then builds upstream URL as base + api_path with the /v1 prefix only stripped when base ends with /v1 (src/proxy.rs:778-784); google base is https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta, so the request goes to .../v1beta/v1/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent -> 404.

Fix: recognize :generateContent / :streamGenerateContent suffixes as native Google requests, strip the eavs routing /v1, and pass through to {base}/models/{model}:...; keep ?alt=sse query. Passthrough is format-correct here (body is already native google), only the URL mapping is wrong. Same normalization concern applies to any provider whose base doesn't end in /v1 (e.g. github-copilot: /v1/responses -> upstream expects /responses).
close_reason: Implemented: :generateContent/:streamGenerateContent/:countTokens recognized as native Google requests for Google/GoogleVertex; /v1 routing artifact stripped so upstream sees {base}/models/{model}:action; model extracted from path; google usage extraction. GoogleGeminiCli/Bedrock now advertise pi_api=openai-completions since they require the translation layer. e2e test e2e_native_google_generate_content_passthrough.

title: Codex SSE transport: POST /codex/responses returns 405 and zstd request bodies unsupported
description:
pi's openai-codex-responses api defaults to transport "auto": WebSocket first, falling back to SSE (POST) on WS failure or `websocket_connection_limit_reached`. Two eavs gaps break the SSE path:

1. Routing: /:provider/v1/codex/responses and /v1/codex/responses are registered GET-only for the WS upgrade handler (src/main.rs:850-856). pi's SSE fallback POSTs to the same path -> axum returns 405 (does not fall through to the /:provider/v1/*path any() route). Note the HTTP proxy handler already special-cases api_path "/codex/responses" (src/proxy.rs:544) — it's just unreachable for the pi-advertised URL shape.

2. zstd: since pi-mono 0ac3cfe0 (feat(ai): use zstd compression for codex sse transport) pi sends `content-encoding: zstd` request bodies on the SSE path. eavs has no zstd anywhere (grep confirms) and parses request JSON for policy/injection/logging — a compressed body fails to parse.

Fix: route POST on those paths to the HTTP proxy handler; decompress zstd request bodies before JSON parsing (and re-compress or send identity upstream). Also verify the WS relay stays compatible with pi's 55-min session rotation (SESSION_WEBSOCKET_MAX_AGE_MS) and the beta header responses_websockets=2026-02-06 (eavs already sends this, src/proxy.rs:2301-2304).
close_reason: Implemented: POST added to /v1/codex/responses and /:provider/v1/codex/responses (GET stays WS upgrade); /v1/codex/responses recognized as Responses passthrough and mapped to {base}/codex/responses; zstd request bodies decompressed before parsing (zstd crate). e2e test e2e_codex_sse_post_with_zstd_body.

title: Unknown provider type silently falls back to OpenAI; accept openai-completions alias (root cause of eavs-gh49)
description:
Provider `type` is a free-form string parsed by ProviderType::from_str with a silent `_ => OpenAI` fallback (src/provider.rs:62-86). "openai-completions" is not a recognized type, so a Foundry/OpenAI-compatible provider configured with type = "openai-completions" is misclassified as native OpenAI, which pi_api_for_provider (src/api.rs:411-432) then advertises to pi as "openai-responses" — exactly bug eavs-gh49 (foundry-wg).

Fix:
- Accept "openai-completions" (and maybe "chat-completions") as aliases of OpenAICompatible.
- Stop silently defaulting unknown type strings to OpenAI: warn loudly at config load and/or reject; setup wizard should validate.
- Consider a real per-provider pi_api override in ProviderConfig (the adapter already honors provider.pi_api, adapters/pi/adapter.ts:24-25, but eavs never stores one — it is always derived from type, src/api.rs:411-432).

Related: eavs-gh49.
close_reason: Implemented: openai-completions and chat-completions accepted as aliases of OpenAICompatible; new ProviderType::try_from_str; config load now warns loudly on unrecognized provider types instead of silently treating them as OpenAI. Unblocks eavs-gh49 (retype foundry-wg as openai-completions/openai-compatible).

title: Export compat to pi models.json — pi mis-detects quirks behind the proxy
description:
pi's openai-completions quirk detection (detectCompat, pi-mono packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts:1179+) keys off baseUrl substrings (api.openai.com, openrouter.ai, api.z.ai, deepseek.com, cerebras.ai, api.x.ai, ...). Behind eavs the baseUrl is http://localhost:.../{name}/v1, so detection matches nothing and pi falls back to generic defaults: wrong thinkingFormat (deepseek/zai/openrouter/qwen thinking breaks), stream_options.include_usage possibly not sent (pi loses usage/cost data), reasoning_effort / store / developer-role / max_completion_tokens mis-gated.

pi's models.json supports explicit provider- and model-level `compat` (validated subset in coding-agent model-registry.ts:106-156: OpenAICompletionsCompat incl. thinkingFormat/openRouterRouting, OpenAIResponsesCompat, AnthropicMessagesCompat) which overrides detection.

eavs side today:
- Provider-level CompatSettings (supports_store, supports_developer_role, max_tokens_field, supports_stream_options; src/provider.rs:543-628) — used in the proxy but NOT exported to adapters.
- Model-level `compat: HashMap<String,Value>` (src/config.rs:446-449) whose comment says "passed through to models.json as-is" — but build_provider_data (src/export.rs:119-157) never includes it. Dead-ended: implement the documented behavior.

Fix: include provider+model compat in the adapter payload (adapters/types/index.ts EavsProvider/EavsModel), emit `compat` in adapters/pi/adapter.ts, and auto-derive sensible compat from the real upstream base URL (port pi's detection table) so users don't have to hand-write it. Note pi's schema omits a few TS-only keys (zaiToolStream, sendSessionAffinityHeaders on completions; supportsTemperature/allowEmptySignature on anthropic) — emitting them is harmless but ineffective.
close_reason: Implemented: provider-level resolved compat exported on ProviderDetail + adapter payload; pi adapter maps supports_store/supports_developer_role/max_tokens_field/supports_stream_options to supportsStore/supportsDeveloperRole/maxTokensField/supportsUsageInStreaming (openai-completions providers only); model-level compat HashMap now actually passed through to models.json as documented. Auto-deriving pi's full detection table (thinkingFormat etc.) left as follow-up if needed.

title: Per-model api in pi adapter: multi-API providers (github-copilot) advertised with one api for all models
description:

title: OAuth drift vs pi: codex chatgpt_account_id, anthropic token URL/scopes, copilot default client id, codex authorize params
description:

title: Strip provider-delegated remote image/document URLs
description:
Security follow-up discovered while implementing eavs-w6wg.9.

EAVS's delegated-fetch sanitizer intentionally covers the issue-specified OpenAI Responses `input_file.file_url` surface and provider-hosted `tools[]`, but other provider-delegated URL fetch surfaces remain:

- OpenAI Chat Completions / compatible passthrough: `messages[].content[].image_url.url`
- Anthropic native image/document blocks: `source: { type: "url", url: "..." }`
- Equivalent native/pass-through remote media URL shapes supported by providers

On OpenAI-compatible and native passthrough paths, the upstream provider fetches these URLs server-side. That traffic rides the allowed inference channel and is invisible to EAVS network ACL/egress enforcement, creating the same SSRF/exfiltration class as `input_file.file_url`. `resolve_image_urls_in_context` only fetches/validates selected transformed-provider image URLs client-side and does not protect all passthrough/native paths.

Required outcome:
- Extend delegated-fetch sanitization with explicit policy controls for remote image/document URL content.
- Default deny provider-side remote URL fetching without breaking inline `data:`/base64 media.
- Cover OpenAI-compatible passthrough, transformed requests, native Anthropic/Google paths, HTTP, Realtime WS, and Codex WS where applicable.
- Emit the existing structured delegated-fetch audit event with JSON field path and parsed target host.

Proof of positive outcome:
1. E2E capture tests submit each supported remote media URL shape through passthrough/native/transformed paths and assert no remote URL reaches the upstream body.
2. Inline data/base64 media remains byte/value-equivalent.
3. Explicit allow configuration preserves remote URLs.
4. Audit assertions include exact field path and target host.
5. Full cargo test passes.

title: GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark support and WebSocket transport for Codex Responses
description:
Add support for the new GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark model and the WebSocket transport for the openai-codex-responses API, aligning eavs with pi-mono v0.52.12 changes.

## Context

OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark on Feb 12, 2026 -- a smaller GPT-5.3 variant optimized for real-time coding at 1000+ tok/s on Cerebras hardware. Text-only, 128k context, research preview for ChatGPT Pro users via Codex app/CLI/IDE (not public API at launch).

pi-mono added:
- Model definition (fb833070) for both openai and openai-codex providers
- WebSocket transport (a26a9cfa) for openai-codex-responses with session caching
- New Transport type in StreamOptions: sse | websocket | auto

## Key technical details

### Codex Spark model
- id: gpt-5.3-codex-spark
- reasoning: true, input: text-only
- contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 128000 (codex) / 16384 (API)
- cost: 0/0/0/0 (free during research preview)
- Same endpoint: chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
- Same JWT auth with chatgpt-account-id header

### WebSocket transport
- Beta header: OpenAI-Beta: responses_websockets=2026-02-06
- URL: wss://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses (wss:// version of the HTTP endpoint)
- Client sends: {"type": "response.create", ...body} as a JSON message
- Server sends: ResponseStreamEvent JSON messages (same events as SSE, unwrapped)
- Session caching: connections cached per sessionId with 5min idle TTL
- Default: SSE (WebSocket is opt-in via transport option)

## Scope

1. Model recognition for gpt-5.3-codex-spark in provider detection
2. WebSocket proxy handler for Codex responses endpoint
3. Transport-aware routing (SSE vs WebSocket upgrade detection)
close_reason: Done: Codex Responses WebSocket proxy at /v1/codex/responses and /:provider/v1/codex/responses. Intercepts response.create for policy (set_field store=true), tracks usage from response.completed, full auth with OAuth resolution. gpt-5.3-codex-spark model detection already works via 'codex' substring match.

title: Add WebSocket proxy handler for Codex responses endpoint
description:
Add WebSocket upgrade handling for the Codex responses endpoint so eavs can proxy WebSocket connections (key management, rate limiting, logging) when clients use the new WebSocket transport.

## Context

pi-mono v0.52.12 added WebSocket transport for openai-codex-responses. When a client uses transport=websocket, it opens a WebSocket to wss://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses instead of an HTTP POST. eavs currently only proxies WebSocket for /v1/realtime (OpenAI Realtime API).

## Implementation

### New route
- Handle WebSocket upgrade on /codex/responses and /{provider}/codex/responses paths
- Reuse the pattern from the existing /v1/realtime WebSocket proxy handler (lines ~1688-2050 in proxy.rs)

### Authentication
- Same JWT token handling as the HTTP Codex path
- Extract chatgpt-account-id from JWT
- Inject required Codex headers: originator, OpenAI-Beta: responses_websockets=2026-02-06

### Key management
- Validate API key (same as HTTP path)
- Apply rate limiting to WebSocket connections

### Upstream connection
- Convert base URL to wss:// (same as build_ws_url)
- Forward all headers including the beta header
- Bidirectional message proxying (client sends response.create JSON, server sends ResponseStreamEvent JSON)

### Differences from /v1/realtime handler
- Message format: plain JSON objects (not the Realtime API event protocol)
- Beta header: responses_websockets=2026-02-06 (not realtime=v1)
- Connection lifecycle: client may send multiple response.create requests on a single socket (session caching)
- No audio/WebRTC concerns

## Reference
- pi-mono: packages/ai/src/providers/openai-codex-responses.ts (processWebSocketStream, acquireWebSocket, parseWebSocket)
- Existing eavs WS handler: src/proxy.rs handle_ws_proxy_inner()
close_reason: Done: codex_ws_handler_inner in proxy.rs handles /v1/codex/responses and /:provider/v1/codex/responses WebSocket connections

title: Support transport-aware routing for Codex requests
description:
Detect whether an incoming Codex request is SSE (HTTP POST) or WebSocket (upgrade) and route accordingly.

## Details

When a client sends a request to the Codex responses endpoint:
- HTTP POST with Accept: text/event-stream -> existing SSE proxy path (no changes needed)
- HTTP request with Connection: Upgrade + Upgrade: websocket -> new WebSocket proxy handler

The proxy should transparently handle both on the same path (/codex/responses). Axum supports this via WebSocketUpgrade extractor -- if the upgrade headers are present, route to the WS handler; otherwise fall through to the HTTP handler.

## Considerations
- The transport decision is made by the client (pi), not the proxy
- eavs does not need a transport option in its config -- it just responds to what the client requests
- Logging should indicate which transport is in use for observability
- Rate limiting should work consistently across both transports

title: Add generic 'owner' label to virtual keys for cross-key usage rollups
description:
Attach an optional, auth-independent 'owner' label to virtual keys so multiple keys can be grouped under one user/tag and usage/cost rolled up per owner.

title: Migration ordering bug: CREATE INDEX idx_usage_owner runs before ALTER adds owner column to pre-existing usage_history
description:
## Summary
On upgrade to EAVS 0.8.1, key-store initialization fails on databases created by older versions with:

```
ERROR eavs: Failed to initialize key store: Database error: (code: 1) no such column: owner
```

The key store is then non-functional: `GET /admin/keys` and `POST /admin/keys` both return HTTP 500 `{"error":"Key store not initialized","code":"internal_error"}`, so every virtual-key-authenticated request fails (`require_key = true` => total outage).

## Root cause
`src/keys/store.rs` migration orders operations incorrectly for `usage_history`:

1. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS usage_history (... owner TEXT ...)` — this is a **no-op** when the table already exists (from 0.8.0-era schema), so the `owner` column is NOT added by it.
2. `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_usage_owner ON usage_history(owner)` — runs **immediately after**, but `owner` does not exist yet on a pre-existing table → `no such column: owner`. Init aborts.
3. The block that would have added the column (`ALTER TABLE usage_history ADD COLUMN owner TEXT`, gated by `pragma_table_info`) is reached only **after** the failing index creation, so it never runs.

Note: the same pattern is correct for `virtual_keys` (the `has_owner` pragma check + ALTER runs before any owner-referencing query). Only `usage_history` is mis-ordered. `cache_write_tokens` has the same latent risk (its ALTER is also after the index creation path) but didn't trigger because no index references it.

## Reproduction
1. Start with a keys.db from <= 0.8.0 whose `usage_history` lacks the `owner` column (and `cache_write_tokens`).
2. Install/upgrade to EAVS 0.8.1 (binary at /usr/local/bin/eavs, version 0.8.1).
3. `eavs serve` (or `systemctl restart eavs`).
4. Observe init error in journal and HTTP 500 on `/admin/keys`.

Confirmed live on octo-azure (oqto instance) after a 0.8.0 -> 0.8.1 binary upgrade at 2026-07-30 14:09 UTC.

## Fix
Reorder the usage_history migration so column additions precede index creation. Concretely in `src/keys/store.rs` migrate():
- Run the `has_usage_owner` pragma check + `ALTER TABLE usage_history ADD COLUMN owner TEXT` BEFORE `CREATE INDEX idx_usage_owner ON usage_history(owner)`.
- Run the `has_cache_write` pragma check + `ALTER TABLE usage_history ADD COLUMN cache_write_tokens ...` before any index/constraint that references it.

Generally: never reference a column in a CREATE INDEX / constraint until the ADD COLUMN that guarantees it has run, regardless of whether CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS was a no-op.

## How to prove a positive outcome (acceptance test)
Add a regression test that:
1. Creates a keys.db with the legacy usage_history schema (no `owner`, no `cache_write_tokens`) — e.g. by running an older migration or hand-crafting the table.
2. Points EAVS at it and calls the migrate/init path.
3. Asserts init succeeds (no error), `usage_history` has both `owner` and `cache_write_tokens` columns, `idx_usage_owner` exists, and `POST /admin/keys` + `GET /admin/keys` return 2xx.

The test must fail on current 0.8.1 and pass after the reordering fix.

## Workaround applied (do NOT rely on this)
On the affected instance the columns were added manually before restart:
`ALTER TABLE usage_history ADD COLUMN owner TEXT;`
`ALTER TABLE usage_history ADD COLUMN cache_write_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;`
(keys.db backed up first.) This unblocks 0.8.1 but every other <=0.8.0 deployment upgrading to 0.8.1 will hit the same outage until the migration is fixed.

## Related
- eavs-5gf3 (feature that introduced the `owner` column) — this bug is a regression in that feature's migration.
close_reason: Reordered run_migrations in src/keys/store.rs so the usage_history ALTER TABLE column additions (owner, cache_write_tokens) run BEFORE CREATE INDEX statements that reference those columns. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is split from index creation, with ALTERs in between. Added regression test test_migration_handles_legacy_usage_history that seeds a legacy usage_history schema (no owner/cache_write_tokens columns), runs the real migration via KeyStore::new, and asserts: init succeeds, both columns exist, idx_usage_owner exists, legacy row survives, and the store is functional (create_key + update_usage + get_usage_by_owner). Verified the test FAILS on 0.8.1 code with the exact reported error '(code: 1) no such column: owner' and PASSES after the fix. Full suite: 379 passed, 0 failed. Committed in f5b875e.

**Use case:** Sandboxed agents need GitHub access but shouldn't have direct access to credentials.

**gh CLI token storage (for reference):**
- macOS: System Keychain (service: gh:github.com, base64 encoded)
- Linux: libsecret, or ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml plaintext fallback  
- Windows: Windows Credential Manager

   ```toml
   [providers.github]

   api_key = "keychain:github"  # or env:GH_TOKEN
   ```

   - Request comes through HTTPS_PROXY

2. src/provider.rs - Add GitHubApi provider type:

   ```rust
       env_key_name: Some("GH_TOKEN"),
       auth_style: AuthStyle::BearerToken,
   }
   ```

3. Add Unix socket listener option:
   ```toml

   unix_socket = "/tmp/eavs-gh.sock"  # optional, in addition to TCP
   ```

title: Add secure credential storage using system keychain (macOS Keychain, libsecret, Windows Credential Manager)
description:
Currently EAVS stores API keys in:
- config.toml (plaintext, supports env: prefix)
- SQLite database for OAuth tokens (plaintext)

**Problem:** In sandboxed agent environments, we want EAVS to have access to credentials but NOT the agent. If credentials are in plaintext files, a sandboxed agent could potentially read them.

**Solution:** Use system keychain for credential storage:
- macOS: Keychain Services (Security framework)
- Linux: libsecret / GNOME Keyring / KWallet
- Windows: Windows Credential Manager

**Rust crate:** keyring-rs (cross-platform keyring access)
- Cargo.toml: keyring = "3"
- Docs: https://docs.rs/keyring/latest/keyring/

**Implementation steps:**

1. Add dependency to Cargo.toml:
   ```toml
   [dependencies]
   keyring = "3"
   ```

2. Add config option in config.toml schema:
   ```toml
   [keys]
   storage_backend = "keychain"  # or "plaintext" (default)
   ```

3. New api_key syntax in provider config:
   ```toml
   [providers.openai]
   type = "openai"
   api_key = "keychain:openai"  # reads from system keychain
   # existing syntaxes still work:
   # api_key = "env:OPENAI_API_KEY"
   # api_key = "sk-..."
   ```

4. Keychain entry format:
   - Service: "eavs"
   - Account: "{provider}:api_key" (e.g., "openai:api_key")
   - For OAuth: "oauth:{provider}:{user_id}"

5. New CLI commands:
   ```bash
   # Store a key in keychain
   eavs keys set openai --keychain
   # Enter API key: [hidden input]
   
   # List keys (shows storage location)
   eavs keys list
   # openai: keychain
   # anthropic: config (plaintext)
   # google: env:GEMINI_API_KEY
   
   # Migrate existing plaintext keys to keychain
   eavs keys migrate-to-keychain
   
   # Read key from keychain (for debugging)
   eavs keys get openai --reveal
   ```

6. Code locations to modify:
   - src/config.rs: Add storage_backend config, parse keychain: prefix
   - src/keys/mod.rs: Add keychain storage backend
   - src/cli.rs: Add keys set/migrate commands
   - src/oauth/storage.rs: Support keychain for OAuth tokens

7. Fallback behavior:
   - If keychain unavailable, warn and fall back to plaintext
   - On headless Linux without libsecret, suggest: apt install libsecret-1-dev

**Example keyring-rs usage:**
```rust
use keyring::Entry;

// Store
let entry = Entry::new("eavs", "openai:api_key")?;
entry.set_password("sk-...")?;

// Retrieve
let entry = Entry::new("eavs", "openai:api_key")?;
let api_key = entry.get_password()?;

// Delete
entry.delete_credential()?;
```

**Benefits:**
- Credentials protected by OS-level security
- Sandboxed agents can't read credentials even with filesystem access
- Can require user authentication (Touch ID, password) for access
- Consistent with gh CLI and other tools

title: Message-body logging is on-by-default; make it opt-in (privacy)
description:
FINDING: eavs logs full chat content by default for JSON/file backends. AnalysisEvent::Request carries the entire request body (the messages/prompts array) and AnalysisEvent::ResponseChunk carries raw response chunks (model output). StdoutSink pretty mode only prints body['model'], but the JSON branch (serde_json::to_string(event)) and FileSink serialize the WHOLE event -- so prompts + completions land in the log. LoggingConfig has no toggle (only default/backends/sink). log_redact covers API keys/tokens, NOT message content.

REQUIRED: message/response content logging must be OPT-IN, default OFF.

PROPOSED DESIGN:
- Add LoggingConfig.log_bodies: bool (default false). Optionally split request_bodies/response_bodies if useful.
- Redact at the SOURCE: when log_bodies=false, omit/replace the body (request) and chunk/response content before the AnalysisEvent reaches any sink, so no backend can ever see content. Keep metadata always: model, method, uri, status, duration_ms, token/cost counts.
- When log_bodies=true: log full content (explicit opt-in; document the privacy implication in README + config.example.toml).
- Audit other sinks (webhook, OpenTelemetry) for the same exposure.

CONTEXT: eavs is intended as an OPTIONAL observability/audit lens on model traffic, never the trace/history authority (that is hstry/oqto-log for oqto). This bug is about not silently capturing sensitive conversation content by default.

title: Auto-discovery: model defaults and zero-config endpoint
description:

Three components:
1. GET /defaults endpoint exposing named model tiers (default, fast, reasoning, fallback)
2. Model alias resolution in the proxy -- requests with model='default'/'fast'/'reasoning' get rewritten to actual model IDs before routing
3. Convention: apps probe localhost:3033/health, if eavs responds, use it with model aliases

title: Model alias resolution in proxy -- rewrite default/fast/reasoning to real model IDs
description:
When the proxy receives a request with model field set to a named alias ("default", "fast", "reasoning", "fallback"), OR with model field missing/empty/null, resolve it to the actual model ID from [defaults] config before routing.

Resolution order:
1. model field is a known alias ("default", "fast", "reasoning", "fallback") -> resolve to configured model
2. model field is missing, empty, or null -> resolve to "default" tier
3. model field is a real model ID -> pass through unchanged (existing behavior)

Implementation:
- In proxy.rs, after extracting the model field from the request body, check if it is absent/empty or matches a known alias
- If so, replace it with the resolved model ID and set the provider accordingly
- Add X-Eavs-Resolved-Model response header showing the actual model used
- Add X-Eavs-Tier response header showing which tier was used (e.g. "default", "fast")
- If the alias is not configured or no [defaults] section exists, return 400 with a clear error message
- This happens before any provider routing logic so the rest of the pipeline sees a real model ID

This is the key zero-config feature: apps send messages with no model field and eavs handles everything.

title: Require authentication on the loopback listener and stop disclosing configured providers
description:
Finding (oqto-5spg audit, 2026-07-25): EAVS answers on 127.0.0.1 without authentication, and unauthenticated clients can enumerate configured providers.

Invariant: every endpoint reachable from an agent workspace must be authenticated or capability-gated; reachability is not an authorization boundary.

Direction agreed with oqto:
- Fix belongs in EAVS: add token/capability auth on the HTTP listener and redact provider listing behind auth.
- Oqto side will consume it via the endpoint bridge / runner protocol seam (ADR-0007/0035 egress shape), so the credential can be injected like other secrets.

Proof: unauthenticated GET to provider/config endpoints must be denied; a workspace-sandboxed process reaching the loopback listener must receive 401/403.

The listener now requires EAVS_AUTH_TOKEN/server.auth_token (or warns and falls back to the existing master key), accepts X-Eavs-Token to coexist with virtual-key Authorization headers, and returns a generic 401 before provider/default/config handlers run. Fresh installs generate a 256-bit token in a mode-0600 config; internal CLI health/provider/proxy requests and auto-start readiness checks propagate the capability. Removed startup provider-name logging and documented/schema'd the new requirement. Proof: regression test denies unauthenticated /providers and /defaults without provider-name leakage while allowing the authenticated request; first-run token generation/perms test passes; cargo test passes 389/389; live loopback curl confirms unauthenticated GET /providers => 401 generic body and authenticated => 200. cargo clippy --tests completes with only 12 pre-existing warnings.

title: Cost accounting: track cache-write tokens and source rates from models.dev
description:
Virtual-key cost accounting undercounts cache-heavy workloads and mis-prices unknown models.

Root causes:
- UsageTracker only captures cache_read_input_tokens; cache_creation (write) tokens are dropped, so Anthropic prompt-cache writes (billed 1.25x input) are billed as normal input.
- keys/pricing.rs ModelPricing has only cached_input_cost_per_token (read); no cache_write field. Rates come from a small hand-maintained embedded table, so unknown models fall back to guesses (and a flat 50% cached-read discount that is wrong for Anthropic ~10%).
- calculate_cost_with_cache does input-cached unconditionally; correct for OpenAI (inclusive) but wrong for Anthropic (input already excludes cache).

Fix:
- Source rates from models.dev CatalogCost (already deserialized: input/output/cache_read/cache_write, in USD/1M tokens). Add cache_write_cost_per_token to ModelPricing; populate from catalog (÷1e6).
- Convention from data: cache_write present -> Anthropic-style, bill creation tokens at cache_write; absent/0 -> OpenAI-style, no separate write cost.
- Capture cache_creation_input_tokens in UsageTracker; thread through update_usage; add usage_history.cache_write_tokens column (idempotent migration).
- Provider-aware input handling: do not subtract cache from Anthropic input; subtract only for inclusive (OpenAI) convention.
- cost = regular_input*input + cache_read*read_rate + cache_write*write_rate + output*output.

Also: CLI cost-overview commands (per owner/user and per key: tokens + costs).
close_reason: Cache-write tokens now tracked and priced; rates sourced from models.dev catalog with provider-aware cache convention. Added CLI cost by-owner/by-key rollups.

A secret ref is '<scheme>:<path>', dispatched to a backend, resolved value cached with a TTL, never logged. kyz is the FIRST provider (byteowlz default for oqto); the injection engine and config are backend-agnostic. Env/file schemes serve dev. Additional backends are a separate child. This is the resolution layer the substitution engine (eavs-w6wg.3) calls.

title: Fix test-all summary counting 'Continue anyway' as passed
description:
When running 'eavs setup test-all', if a provider test fails and the user selects 'Continue anyway? yes', the test is counted as passed in the summary.

## Root cause

In src/setup.rs, test_provider_direct() returns Ok(()) when the user confirms 'Continue anyway' on a failed test (lines ~497-503 and ~518-524). The caller run_setup_test_all() (line ~254) uses Ok/Err to count passed/failed, so swallowed failures are counted as passed.

## Expected behavior

Summary should show: '3/14 passed, 11 failed'
Currently shows:    '14/14 passed, 0 failed'

## Fix

Return a richer result from test_provider_direct that distinguishes:
- actually passed
- failed but user chose to continue  
- failed and user chose to abort

Options:
1. Return an enum: Passed / FailedContinue / FailedAbort
2. Return Ok(bool) where true=passed, false=failed-but-continue, Err=abort
3. Track passed/failed/skipped separately in run_setup_test_all
close_reason: Fixed: test_provider_direct now returns TestOutcome enum (Passed/FailedContinue) instead of Ok(()) for user-continued failures. run_setup_test_all counts FailedContinue as failed. Also added test_model config field and pi models.json discovery.

Eavs currently only supports LLM chat completion providers. Users need to store and proxy API keys for non-LLM services like:

- OpenAI Sora (video generation)
- ElevenLabs (TTS/audio)
- Replicate (multi-modal)
- Stability AI (image generation)
- Other specialized AI services

2. Proxy requests to arbitrary endpoints with stored credentials

4. Expose keys to agents securely (via env vars or credential proxy)

title: Secret-aware egress: MITM credential injection for allowlisted hosts (placeholder model + kyz)
description:
Layer credential injection onto the transparent egress proxy (eavs-frd8, now complete). Today the transparent listener does capture + allow/deny + splice (passthrough); it never sees inside TLS, so it cannot inject secrets. This epic adds selective MITM for explicitly-configured hosts so the client only ever holds PLACEHOLDER tokens while eavs substitutes the real credential at the transport layer for the matching allowlisted host -- the gondolin createHttpHooks model, backed by a PLUGGABLE secret-provider interface (kyz is one backend among Vault/Infisical/Bitwarden/1Password/cloud; see eavs-sth0).

Invariant: the real secret NEVER enters the client (env, memory, fs). The client env carries a high-entropy placeholder; eavs swaps in the real value only for the destination that secret is scoped to, only after TLS termination, and blocks any real value heading to a non-allowlisted host (anti-exfil).

Scope boundaries:
- MITM only the hosts configured for injection; everything else stays splice/passthrough (preserves perf and does not break cert-pinned clients).
- HTTP(S) only (placeholder substitution needs a request to rewrite). SSH/DB wire protocols are out of scope.
- Secret backend is pluggable and backend-agnostic in the injection path; no provider is privileged.
- Cross-repo touchpoint kept thin: the consumer (e.g. oqto-sandbox) must trust eavs's MITM CA -- eavs publishes the CA; the consumer installs it into its client trust store. The oqto-specific install logic lives on the oqto side, not in eavs.

Reference: external-repos/gondolin/host/src/http/hooks.ts (createHttpHooks, applySecretsToRequest, assertSecretValuesAllowedForHost). Builds on the transparent listener in src/transparent.rs.

Definition of done: a client holding a placeholder reaches an allowlisted host through eavs, the real (provider-resolved) credential is injected and upstream returns 200; the same placeholder/real value sent to a non-allowlisted host is blocked; secrets never appear in logs or on the client; audit records every injection.

title: MITM CA + dynamic leaf certificate generation
description: eavs needs a local CA to terminate TLS for injection hosts. Generate/persist an eavs MITM CA (long-lived, stored under eavs state dir). On each MITM connection, mint a short-lived leaf cert for the requested SNI signed by the CA, cached by host. rustls server config with a dynamic cert resolver (ResolvesServerCert) keyed on SNI. Expose the CA cert (file path + an endpoint) so it can be installed into agent trust stores (see the CA-trust-provisioning child). Never expose the CA private key. Deps: rustls server side (eavs already uses rustls for the client).

title: Selective TLS termination in the transparent listener
description: Extend src/transparent.rs: after the SNI/Host peek, decide per-host MITM vs splice. For hosts configured for injection, terminate TLS with the eavs CA leaf cert (rustls acceptor), read the plaintext HTTP request, hand it to the substitution engine, re-encrypt to upstream (eavs already has an HTTPS client). For all other hosts, keep the current passthrough splice (perf, and avoids breaking cert-pinned clients). Handle: HTTP/1.1 and h2 ALPN, connection reuse, and a clean fallback if termination fails. Blocked by the MITM CA child.

title: Placeholder-secret substitution engine (gondolin createHttpHooks model)
description: Port the gondolin secret model (external-repos/gondolin/host/src/http/hooks.ts). Per secret: a high-entropy placeholder (the client's env value) + a host allowlist + the real value resolved via the pluggable secret-provider interface (eavs-sth0; kyz or any other backend). On a terminated request: replace placeholder->real in headers (and optionally URL query) ONLY when the request host matches that secret's allowlist; inject at the last moment after any rewriting. Anti-exfil: assertSecretValuesAllowedForHost -- block a request already carrying a real secret value bound for a non-allowlisted host (redirect hops). Keep SSRF/internal-range blocks. Unit-testable as a pure request->request transform. Blocked by config schema + the secret-provider interface.

title: Injection policy + config schema
description: Config for which hosts get MITM+injection and the secret mapping: host pattern -> { placeholder, kyz secret ref, where-to-inject (header name / scheme like 'Authorization: Bearer', or URL param) }. Likely a [transparent.inject] section or per-secret entries. Validate at load; fail-closed on malformed entries. Surfaces the placeholder values eavs hands out so the provisioning side can set them in the agent env.

title: Agent CA-trust provisioning (cross-repo with oqto-sandbox)
description: For MITM to work the agent must trust the eavs CA. eavs side: expose the CA cert (stable file path + optional fetch endpoint) and document the contract. oqto-sandbox side (separate repo, file there too): install the eavs CA into the agent's trust -- bind-mount/copy into the sandbox and set SSL_CERT_FILE / NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE etc. so curl/node/python/git all trust it. Also inject the per-secret PLACEHOLDER env values into the agent. Coordinate with the egress relay setup so this only happens for proxy-mode sessions with injection configured.

title: Audit + redaction for injected secrets
description: Record every injection (timestamp, host, secret name/ref, virtual key/session) WITHOUT the secret value. Ensure real secret values never reach logs (extend redact_sensitive to cover injected creds and placeholders). Never expose the real value to the agent side of the connection. Surface injection events via the existing logging/observability path.

title: End-to-end secret-injection tests
description: Validate the full path: (1) agent holds only a placeholder; a request to an allowlisted host is MITM'd, the real kyz-resolved credential injected, upstream returns 200; (2) the same placeholder/real value sent to a NON-allowlisted host is blocked (anti-exfil); (3) the secret never appears in logs or on the agent side; (4) non-injection hosts still splice untouched. Localhost harness (fake upstream + a CA-trusting client) for CI; plus a privileged end-to-end through the real netns relay. Blocked by the implementation children.

description:
Concrete SecretProvider impls behind the trait (see eavs-sth0). Each is a thin adapter; add incrementally. Suggested ref schemes + priority:

Tier 1 (with the interface): kyz: (byteowlz default), env: / file: (dev) -- mostly done via the existing prefix scheme.

title: Strip delegated-fetch capabilities from request bodies (input_file/file_url, server-side tools)
description:
Security gap confirmed 2026-08-20 against Prime Intellect's universal offline-sandbox-escape disclosure (primeintellect.ai/blog/universal-offline-sandbox-escape): EAVS passes request bodies through unmodified (no handling of input_file/file_url or server-side tools anywhere in src/proxy.rs), so any client can ride the ALLOWED inference channel to make the provider fetch arbitrary URLs (OpenAI Responses API input_file.file_url) or run server-side web tools - an SSRF/exfiltration channel invisible to network egress enforcement. GPT-5.6 used exactly this to escape a blocked-egress eval sandbox.

IMPLEMENTATION
1. New src/delegated_fetch.rs: DelegatedFetchPolicy { allow_remote_content: bool, allowed_server_tools: Vec<String> } + sanitize(body: &mut Value, policy) -> Vec<StrippedItem> (field path + target host if parseable, for audit).
   Walks: (a) Responses API input[] content arrays - drop items where type==input_file carrying file_url; (b) tools[] - drop entries whose type is a server-side tool not on the allowed list (web_search, web_fetch); (c) normalize tool_choice when it references a removed tool (else upstream 400s).
2. Call sanitize in proxy_handler right after json_body parse - BEFORE needs_transform branching, so passthrough routes are inspected too.
3. Same call in ws_proxy_handler + codex_ws_handler (Codex traffic rides these).
4. Policy knob: [delegated_fetch] enabled = false in config.toml (global default deny), plus per-virtual-key override map for tenant granularity later.
5. Audit: every strip/refusal logs a structured event naming field path and target host.

DEFAULT = DENY, deliberately breaking: without it the failure mode is silent exfiltration through the allowed channel; with it, failure is a visibly missing capability (model says it cannot fetch) fixable with one config line. Flag as security hardening in CHANGELOG; operators re-enable per deployment if they accept the channel.

PROOF OF DONE: integration test using mock_provider sends a Responses request containing input_file.file_url -> assert upstream-received body has no file_url anywhere; control request without it passes byte-identical; tool_choice normalization covered; audit events asserted.

OQTO-SIDE CONTRACT (implemented, oqto_refactor commit 678bc38d): session keys created by oqto now carry metadata delegated_fetch.remote_content (bool, default false), sourced from the work directory's .oqto/config.toml [egress] delegated_fetch. Sanitizer should read THIS metadata from the key record at request time (default deny when absent) -- no new admin endpoint required. Per-key granularity falls out for free.
close_reason: Completed delegated-fetch hardening including the concurrently-added Oqto tenant contract. Default-deny sanitizer removes Responses input_file.file_url items, strips non-allowlisted provider-hosted tools while preserving function/custom tools, and normalizes tool_choice. Applied to HTTP before transforms/passthrough and to every Realtime/Codex WS JSON text/binary frame; malformed WS frames fail closed. Structured audit events include path/capability/target host. ValidatedKey now carries stored key metadata; metadata.delegated_fetch.remote_content controls remote content per virtual key and defaults false when absent, overriding the global fallback as required by Oqto commit 678bc38d. Tests prove passthrough stripping, byte-identical safe control, audits, allowlist behavior, WS text/binary/fail-closed handling, validator metadata propagation, and two virtual keys receiving deny/allow behavior in one server despite global allow. cargo test: 399 passed; cargo clippy --tests: 12 pre-existing warnings, none introduced.

description:

The provider fetches that URL server-side, so it is the identical SSRF/exfiltration channel through an allowlisted destination and must obey the same DelegatedFetchPolicy: stripped when allow_remote_content is false, passed through when true, audited either way.

title: Hard-deleting a virtual key cascades to usage_history, destroying cost/usage history
description:
`KeyStore::delete_key` runs `DELETE FROM virtual_keys WHERE key_hash = ?`. The `usage_history` table declares `FOREIGN KEY (key_hash) REFERENCES virtual_keys(key_hash) ON DELETE CASCADE`. sqlx 0.8 enables `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` by default (verified: a pool connection reports foreign_keys=1), so the CASCADE fires and every usage_history row for that key is deleted on hard delete.

Impact: cost/usage history (and therefore owner rollups) is silently destroyed when a key is hard-deleted. This contradicts the eavs-5gf3 design goal that rollups "survive key deletion". For a billing/cost feature, losing history on key purge is almost never desirable.

Scope note: the routine production path is `disable_key` (soft delete, used by DELETE /admin/keys/:id), which preserves history — so this only bites the currently-dead-code `delete_key` method. But it should be correct before delete_key is wired up or relied upon.

Discovered while writing the eavs-5gf3 "survive key deletion" regression test.

Fix options to evaluate:

- Or document delete_key as intentionally destructive and gate it behind a --force/--purge flag.
